data.narrative:
Electric Hydrogen, a Series C climate and energy company founded by Raffi Garabedian and David Eaglesham, is currently valued at $1.0B post-money following $700M in total raised capital. The peer universe comprises one public company and eight private firms in the same sector and stage, including Redwood Materials, KoBold Metals, and Amogy.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, grounded in the $1.0B last post-money valuation, applied a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C to later-stage step-ups, yielding $1.7B. Peer-median analysis examined three same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables: Redwood Materials at $6.0B (Series D), KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median across these three peers is $3.0B, with a range of $700M to $6.0B.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $1.4B (low) to $3.4B (high), with a median of $2.3B. The current $1.0B valuation sits below the derived range, reflecting either a discount to comparable-stage peers or undervaluation relative to forward progression norms. Key uncertainties include the broad dispersion in peer valuations ($700M to $6.0B), limited sample size, and stage heterogeneity within the peer set.
